subject: NOVA: Indemnity carveout for AI-generated output — scope and notice mechanics
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@novaprod.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; James Li <james.li@novaprod.com>
Cc: novaprod-counsel@lawfirmllp.com
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity carveout for AI-generated output — follow-up and redlines attached

Kimberly,

Thanks for the call today. As discussed with our legal team, Novaprod is comfortable with Redwood taking responsibility for third-party infringement claims where the asserted infringement arises from code or data that Redwood supplied or included in the model.

However, Novaprod needs clarity on two items before we can proceed to signature:

1) A specific carveout for customer-provided prompts and content that cause the model to output infringing materials (Novaprod will not ask Redwood to indemnify outputs triggered solely by Novaprod content).
2) A clear notice-and-cooperation process with a 10-business-day window for Novaprod to provide evidence and preserve logs, plus our ability to suspend the affected integration while the claim is assessed.

Attached are our suggested redlines (Novaprod-Requested-Redlines.docx). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the carveout language and the mechanics around logs/evidence. If there are any proposed alternatives (insurance offset, escrow, or cap adjustments) let us know.

We appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday so our procurement timeline stays on track.

Best,
Sarah Lewis
Director, Legal Operations
Nova Productivity, Inc.

Attachment: Novaprod-Requested-Redlines.docx (docx, 48KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@novaprod.com>, James Li <james.li@novaprod.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Indemnity carveout for AI-generated output — follow-up and redlines attached

Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and redlines. Quick acknowledgement: we received the doc and are reviewing internally.

Two quick notes from product/legal that will affect our response:
- Redwood takes customer prompts/inputs seriously as an allocation of responsibility; we generally resist an unconditional carveout because some prompt templates are provided by Redwood (examples: starter prompts, persona templates) and we also offer managed prompt engineering services.
- On evidence and logs: we can commit to preserving runtime request logs for 90 days (extendable by SOW) and will accept a notice-based preservation obligation, but we need to avoid an open-ended duty to retain or produce raw model weights/training data.

I'll loop Karthik (contracts) and Grace (customer success / support SLA) to propose specific language and proposed fallback (insurance offset plus limited cap for AI-output claims). Will aim to send a proposed compromise redline set tomorrow morning.

Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NOVA: Indemnity carveout for AI-generated output — scope and notice mechanics

Kim — attaching a draft we discussed. High level:

1) Proposed carveout language: Redwood will not be liable for claims solely caused by Customer-provided inputs, except where Redwood (i) provided the prompt templates that were used as-is without modification, or (ii) performed prompt engineering services under a SOW that resulted in the offending output.

2) Evidence-preservation: Redwood will retain request/response logs for 90 days and preserve them for 180 days upon receiving a written notice of claim. We propose a 14-business-day initial preservation window (to allow CS to perform a preliminary triage) rather than your 10 days; that seems operationally realistic.

3) Cap and offsets: propose AI-output claims be subject to the order form liability cap (monetary cap tied to the order value) with a carveout for willful misconduct and a limited insurance offset (Redwood's liability reduced by available insurance proceeds).

Please review the attached compromise redline (rdw-proposed-redline-novaprod.docx). Grace — can you confirm the operational feasibility of the 14-business-day preservation plus a short suspension path?

Karthik
Sr. Contracts Counsel

Attachment: rdw-proposed-redline-novaprod.docx (docx, 62KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@novaprod.com>, novaprod-counsel@lawfirmllp.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NOVA: Indemnity carveout for AI-generated output — scope and notice mechanics

Sarah / counsel — thanks for your patience. After internal review we've prepared a compromise set of edits intended to balance operational realities with Nova's procurement concerns. Key points: 

- Carveout: Redwood will not indemnify claims arising solely from customer-provided inputs, provided that the customer did not use Redwood-delivered prompt templates unmodified and that no Redwood prompt-engineering SOW applied to the integration. We added a short definition for "Redwood-provided prompt templates" to avoid ambiguity.

- Preservation window: Redwood will preserve request/response logs for 90 days by default and, upon receiving a written claim notice, will preserve related logs for 180 days. We can agree to a 14-business-day window for Novaprod to deliver evidence and an initial triage package; if additional preservation is required we will execute a confirmation SOW or reasonable cost recovery.

- Suspension: Novaprod may request a temporary suspension of the specific integration pending triage; Redwood will evaluate in good faith and may suspend only where there is a reasonable likelihood of material infringement harm. This is intended to avoid broad unilateral suspensions that disrupt other customers.

- Cap and offsets: AI-output indemnity claims will sit within the order form liability cap, with Redwood's liability reduced by any applicable insurance proceeds (insurance offset). Exceptions remain for willful misconduct and gross negligence.

Next steps: 1) If this read is acceptable to Nova, am happy to send a clean tracked/redline for signature; 2) if you need a shorter preservation window we can discuss cost/reliability tradeoffs (e.g., longer archival retention at higher fee).

Please see the attached redline (rdw-technical-and-legal-redline.pdf) and let me know whether you want a call to finalize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rdw-technical-and-legal-redline.pdf (pdf, 84KB)
